name: Fired ability "target X has base power and toughness" / "becomes … in addition" — on the target, not the source
notes: In a fired ability an effect with no target restriction is taken for the source's own and pinned to it (_pinAbilityEffectsToSource). generalBasePTRegex and addTypeRegex gave a single "target X" subject no restriction, so Gigantomancer's "Target creature you control has base power and toughness 7/7" made Gigantomancer 7/7 and showed no target dropdown; likewise Neurok Transmuter, Doc Ock and Rootwise Survivor. Both parsers now give every "target X" subject its restriction, except one that _addAbilityPseudo wrote for a pronoun as a guess ("it" -> "target Pirate" from Coercive Recruiter's trigger condition, where the real target is any creature): the pseudo-permanent lists those subjects in _guessedTargetSubjects, saved as guessedTargetSubjects with the fired ability because a restored board re-parses the already rewritten text. A save without the list keeps the old behaviour. Each ability here is fired once with a target and once with none; with none picked the source must stay as printed. Rootwise Survivor also lost "It gains haste": haveAbilityRegex measured its overlap with the add-type sentence from the line start instead of from its own sentence. A pronoun after a target the effect names is written out as that target (_abilityTargetBefore, cards-helpers.js), so every parser reads the real target and nothing is left to guess: Coercive Recruiter's "it" is "target creature" and takes a non-Pirate; Excava's "It's a 1/1 Spirit creature" is "target artifact, creature, or non-Aura enchantment", takes a creature or an enchantment and is not pinned to Excava when no target is picked. The nearest permanent target before the pronoun is used, past a targeted player (Ms. Bumbleflower: "target opponent draws a card. Put a +1/+1 counter on target creature. It gains flying"), and a target named by subtype counts (Admiral Brass: "target Pirate creature card … It has base power and toughness 4/4. It gains haste"; Tyvar Kell: "up to one target Elf … It gains deathtouch"). Sensei Golden-Tail's "That creature gains bushido 1 and becomes a Samurai" needed the numbered keyword read off the add-type subject. Only a pronoun with no target before it is still a guess.
